selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1 (baseline enforcement)
selected_evidence.summary: cron.allow initially missing; after creating opsadmin and writing /etc/cron.allow with root+opsadmin, root and opsadmin successfully install crontabs while an unlisted test user is explicitly denied by crontab's PAM/allow-file check.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60, crond active, and correct /etc/cron.allow contents prior to restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out (node offline), then succeeded with a new boot_id 313f7785-4c09-4785-830e-38fb3791805e, proving an actual restart occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: post-restart recovery of required service/data (cron access control)
selected_evidence.summary: After restart, crond is active, /etc/cron.allow still lists only root and opsadmin, both can schedule cron jobs, and a newly created non-allowed user is still denied, confirming the configuration persisted and is enforced.

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== step: create opsadmin user =="
if ! id opsadmin >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsadmin
fi
PASS=$(openssl rand -base64 18)
echo "opsadmin:${PASS}" | chpasswd
echo "opsadmin created" 

echo "== step: create a throwaway test user for negative test =="
if ! id crontestuser >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  useradd -m -s /bin/bash crontestuser
fi
TPASS=$(openssl rand -base64 18)
echo "crontestuser:${TPASS}" | chpasswd

echo "== step: write cron.allow =="
printf 'root\nopsadmin\n' > /etc/cron.allow
chown root:root /etc/cron.allow
chmod 644 /etc/cron.allow
cat /etc/cron.allow

echo "== step: remove cron.deny if present (allow file takes precedence but keep clean) =="
rm -f /etc/cron.deny

echo "== verify: root can install crontab =="
echo '* * * * * /bin/true' | crontab -u root - 
crontab -u root -l

echo "== verify: opsadmin can install crontab =="
su -s /bin/sh opsadmin -c "echo '* * * * * /bin/true' | crontab -" 
su -s /bin/sh opsadmin -c "crontab -l"

echo "== verify: crontestuser (not allowed) is denied =="
set +e
OUT=$(su -s /bin/sh crontestuser -c "echo '* * * * * /bin/true' | crontab -" 2>&1)
RC=$?
set -e
echo "rc=$RC"
echo "$OUT"
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: crontestuser was able to install a crontab"
  exit 1
else
  echo "PASS: crontestuser denied as expected"
fi

echo "== cleanup test crontabs (keep root/opsadmin entries minimal - remove test entries) =="
crontab -u root -r || true
su -s /bin/sh opsadmin -c "crontab -r" || true

echo "== cleanup test user =="
userdel -r crontestuser 2>/dev/null || true

echo "DONE"
